title: Philadelphia Fed November 2026 Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey — 8:30 a.m. ET, the missing November instance of a series this calendar already tracks three times
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 131,096 bytes) — the Philadelphia Fed's own release calendar, whose embedded structured data carries the row 'November Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey | Nov 19 2026 | 8:30 a.m.' The same payload's other 2026 MBOS rows are the ones the existing philly-fed-mfg-2026-09-17, philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15 and philly-fed-mfg-2026-12-17 entries already rest on, so this is the identical surface at the identical reliability, not a new class of source. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own release schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only). Discovered 2026-09-09 in the never-assessed initial research of survey-of-professional-forecasters-q4-2026-11-16
notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the survey-of-professional-forecasters-q4-2026-11-16 initial-research adjacency sweep on 2026-09-09. Filed because it is a HOLE IN A SERIES THIS REPO ALREADY TRACKS, not a new instrument: philly-fed-mfg-2026-09-17.json, philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15.json and philly-fed-mfg-2026-12-17.json all exist and carry researched ledgers, and the November edition between October's and December's simply is not on the shelf. The Philadelphia Fed calendar payload that dated this sweep's own event enumerates 17 Philadelphia Fed releases in November 2026 and the MBOS is one of them, at 8:30 a.m. on 2026-11-19. Corridor value is concrete rather than notional: philly-fed-mfg-2026-12-17's ledger and philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25's ledger both turn on the MBOS prices-paid diffusion series, and PIES's own construction rule (established by that ledger, 4 for 4) is that PIES publishes the calendar day after the quarter's NBOS, with the MBOS response window closing 'the Monday prior to publication' — so the 11-19 MBOS is a dated INPUT to the 11-25 PIES print that this calendar currently cannot reference. It also sits three days after this proposer's own event and one day after fomc-minutes-2026-11-18 (medium, confirmed). Impact LOW and symbols [] provisionally, matched to the three existing philly-fed-mfg entries rather than re-litigated by a lane that does not own them. Whoever writes the canonical file owns (a) re-verifying the date and the 8:30 a.m. time against an MBOS-specific release page rather than the shared calendar row — noting the incidental finding recorded by philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25 that the calendar's `?release=` query string is CLIENT-SIDE and every filtered URL returns the same 131,096-byte whole-calendar body — and (b) deciding whether the November edition inherits its siblings' tier or whether landing inside the pre-blackout window changes it. A DECLINE with reasoning recorded is an acceptable outcome. This is a PROPOSAL and an ESTIMATE: it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the proposing ledger registers no forward test that depends on it.
